title: See & Spray targeted applications save 28.4-62.4% of postemergence herbicide with weed control of 93% or more in Arkansas and Mississippi trials
summary: Arkansas-Mississippi trials (2021-2022) with Blue River co-authors: targeted sprays matched broadcast weed control within 1% while saving 28.4% to 62.4% of postemergence herbicide.
account: University of Arkansas weed scientists and Blue River Technology agronomists ran four site-years of randomized complete block trials in 2021 and 2022 at the Northeast Research and Extension Center in Keiser, Arkansas, and Stoneville R&D in Greenville, Mississippi, comparing John Deere See & Spray machine-vision targeted applications with traditional broadcast programs in glyphosate/glufosinate/dicamba-resistant soybean, using a preemergence residual followed by early-postemergence dicamba and mid-postemergence glufosinate. Targeted applications gave control comparable to broadcast, with at most a 1% decrease in efficacy and overall control of 93% or more for Palmer amaranth, broadleaf signalgrass, morningglory and purslane species, reduced soybean injury by at most 5 percentage points without a yield increase, and on average saved 28.4% to 62.4% of postemergence herbicide, with narrower nozzle angles spraying less area. The paper was published online on 15 November 2024, the date used here; it is a research trial, not a commercial farm deployment.
purpose: Detect weeds with machine vision and apply herbicide only where weeds are present, reducing herbicide use while maintaining control.
system: John Deere See & Spray (machine-vision targeted sprayer)
deployer: University of Arkansas and Stoneville R&D field trials (Keiser, AR and Greenville, MS)
taxonomy_note: Field-trial evaluation, so general benefit with null depths. Peer-reviewed in Weed Technology; three of seven authors are Blue River Technology employees, so the paper is marked as written by the makers while the lead authors are at the University of Arkansas.

ratings.reason: Savings of 28.4-62.4% on postemergence herbicide were measured in trial plots; no grower's costs or outcomes are documented.
Reduced herbicide volume is a trial result; no environmental outcome off-plot is measured.

ai_role.statement: The machine-vision sprayer decided where to spray; the comparison with broadcast programs is a randomized trial with consistent herbicides and rates. Savings depended on nozzle angle and machine settings. Co-authored by the maker's agronomists with university weed scientists.

evidence.citation: Avent TH, Norsworthy JK, Patzoldt WL, Schwartz-Lazaro LM, Houston MM, Butts TR, Vazquez AR. Comparing herbicide application methods with See & Spray technology in soybean. Weed Technology 38:e74 (2024). doi:10.1017/wet.2024.70
evidence.title: Comparing herbicide application methods with See & Spray technology in soybean
evidence.quote: On average, targeted sprays saved a range of 28.4% to 62.4% on postemergence herbicides.

produced_by: Herbicide-resistant soybean with a PRE residual, EPOST dicamba and MPOST glufosinate
Four site-years (2021-2022) in a randomized complete block design
must_hold: The specific machine settings and nozzle angles used
